_comment: SER-001 comes in when DV-100's "Do you want the sheriff or marshal to serve the papers ... for free?" is answered Yes (papers_served_by_sheriff_yes). It is the filer's form; the sheriff completes only the file number. Most of it the packet already knows, so those fields carry the names of the questions that ask them and are declared here only so the form compiles on its own: DV-100 items 1 and 2 (names, mailing address, lawyer, gender, race, age and date of birth), DV-100 item 9 (firearms), DV-110 item 2 (height, weight, hair, eyes, and the home address behind its knows_restrained_person_address gate) and CLETS-001 item 1 (nicknames, telephone, marks, vehicle, language). They are written as the plain questions or the same named declarations those forms use, so in the packet each collapses into the one that asked it first - SER-001 has to come after DV-110 and CLETS-001 for that. Four boxes are true whenever SER-001 is in the packet and carry the Yes that brings it in; the home box carries the Yes of DV-110's address gate; both are attachmentTargets, boxes another form's answer ticks, so neither is asked here. What SER-001 asks that nothing else does: the county, the picture, the rest of the safety checklist, gate codes and best times, jail, a second address, and item 5.

autofill.why: Item 2c asks for the case name, "example: Garcia v. Smith" - the filer against the person to be restrained, both already named on DV-100 items 1 and 2.
Item 3a(3), "Date of birth or age". DV-100 item 2 asks both; the box gets the date of birth and the age, or whichever one was given.
Item 3a(3), "Vehicle (type, model, year, color, plate number)". CLETS-001 item 1 asks the type, model, year and plate; they are carried over instead of typed twice.
A signature date has one correct answer and the form already knows it.
The printed name under the signature is the name given in item 2a.

ser001_type_of_papers._why: Item 5a asks what type of court papers the sheriff is serving. In this packet it is always a domestic violence restraining order - that is what SER-001 is here for - so the words are written whenever there is a person to serve. Two conditions with the same words, so either one is enough and the words appear once.

ser001_forms_to_serve._why: Item 5b lists the forms to serve. The packet knows them: DV-109 with DV-100, DV-110 and a blank DV-120 always (the same set DV-200 item 4a and 4b print), and each attachment exactly when the answer that brings it in was given. CLETS-001 is confidential and never served, so it is not listed. FL-150 is served with a blank FL-150 whenever the packet makes it (either support box), and RA-010 whenever the filer will attend by phone or video.

_orderNote: The order the filer meets the fields. Without it the county (item 1) came first, before the person or the address it depends on; it is asked once the addresses are known.
